title: A section of a separated smooth relative curve is Cartier
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism] which is smooth of relative dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $\sigma:S\to X$ satisfy $f\circ\sigma=\operatorname{id}_S$. Then $\sigma$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and its image is an effective Cartier divisor: the quasi-coherent ideal defining that closed subscheme is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. No Noetherian hypothesis on $S$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 067R, lemma-section-smooth-regular-immersion, in relative dimension one; the fibre regular sequence in its proof has length one. Closedness is the section property of a separated morphism.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion] to $p=f$ and $s=\sigma$. The separatedness of $f$ and the equation $f\circ\sigma=\operatorname{id}_S$ are exactly its hypotheses. Thus $\sigma$ is a closed immersion. Regard $D=S$, equipped with this closed immersion $\sigma:D\hookrightarrow X$, as a closed subscheme of $X$; its structure morphism $D\to S$ is the identity, not merely a bijection on points.

The morphism $D\to S$ is finite locally free, as defined in [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Indeed, over each affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$ it is the identity $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}A$: the algebra $A$ is a free $A$-module with basis $1$, so it is finite; tensoring with it is naturally the identity functor on $A$-modules, so it is flat; and it is a finitely presented $A$-algebra with no generators and no relations. This argument works for every commutative ring $A$.

source.place: Tag 0B9D, lemma-divisors-on-curves, condition (1); identity morphism verified directly

proof.text: Apply implication $(1)\Rightarrow(2)$ of [lem-pc-cartier-criterion] to the closed subscheme $D\subseteq X$. Its ambient morphism is the given smooth $f:X\to S$ of relative dimension $1$, and Step 2 proves the finite locally free hypothesis on $D\to S$. It follows that $D$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor on $X/S$. This implication in the cited statement is unconditional: the locally Noetherian hypothesis there concerns only $(4)\Rightarrow(3)$, and properness concerns only $(2)\Rightarrow(1)$; neither is being used.

By [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier], the conclusion of Step 3 includes that $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor. In terms of its defining quasi-coherent ideal, [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] says precisely that on an open cover this ideal has one generator which is a non-zero-divisor. This is the ideal of the closed subscheme defined by $\sigma$, since $D=S$ with closed immersion $\sigma$ throughout. On the complement of its image the ideal is the whole structure sheaf, generated by the non-zero-divisor $1$. This proves the asserted Cartier property on all of $X$, with no Noetherian assumption on $S$.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0B9D, lemma-divisors-on-curves, (1) implies (2), applied to a section closed by Schemes Tag 01KT. The rank-one identity calculation is written out.
